title: Project Abstract
notes: Existing SGG baseline: https://github.com/HHS/simpler-grants-gov/blob/48d93f882c63a711bdec4b16e3150d1293cdff43/api/src/form_schema/forms/project_abstract/1/0/form_json.py . Paths, attachment UUID transport and source XML targets are compared with this revision; tests and rule definitions are inventoried separately.

Source PDF was rendered and reviewed along with DAT labels, help, business rules and XSD structure. Instructions are carried on a nonempty section so they remain visible in the current form-plan view.
The spec_id links the maintained TypeSpec definition and layout. Authored examples now live in TypeSpec; the Data tab shows actual preview answers. Source-shaped XSD models are checked independently.

Attachment controls use a library-only UUID reference editor through the existing renderer registry. They preserve application ID transport and never upload files or claim content, existence or ownership verification.

Attachment XML export is not enabled: file metadata resolution and source-only wrappers require the shared XML mapping work. No incomplete UUID-as-file transform is emitted; this is a definition/preview PR, not a submission-ready migration.
risks: Pinned SGG expiration date is 12/31/2026; the retrieved DAT and PDF say 08/31/2029. Preserve current source metadata in this proposal and confirm the registration update separately.
The one-page and confidentiality instructions are document-content obligations. The existing upload widget and UUID schema do not enforce them.

Synthetic UUID examples are shape illustrations only. Actual uploads, existence/ownership checks, file constraints, XML attachment metadata, application context and submission behavior remain service/runtime obligations. Do not replace UUIDs with invented file descriptors.

children.label: Project Abstract File
children.help_text: The Project Abstract must not exceed one page and must contain a summary of the proposed activity suitable for dissemination to the public.  It should be a self-contained description of the project and should contain a statement of objectives and methods to be employed.  It should be informative to other persons working in the same or related fields and insofar as possible understandable to a technically literate lay reader.  This Abstract must not include any proprietary/confidential information.
